myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: Skinner turns south in this volume, gathering the legends of the Southern states — plantation ghosts, Civil War phantoms, and tales of the old colonial coast. The stories carry the region's particular atmosphere of heat, history, and haunting. A rich sampling of Southern folklore from America's great collector of local legend.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-tostad: This 1913 reference article on Alonso Tostado — El Tostado, the learned Bishop of Avila. Florentine Bechtel praises his vast commentaries. His folios amazed the scholars. The schools marveled at his memory. Spain's prodigy of learning. His works fill twenty-seven folio volumes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonzo-de-alv: This 1913 reference piece on Alonso de Alvarado — the conquistador of Peru. Adolph Bandelier tells his campaigns. He fought with Pizarro's brothers. The Andes knew his iron march. A captain of the Peruvian conquest. His name marks the Peruvian highlands. His sword served three Peruvian campaigns.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-de-al: A 1913 entry on Antonio de Alcedo — the Spanish geographer of America. Adolph Bandelier notes his great Diccionario. His volumes mapped the New World. The colonies' story filled his pages. The geographer of the Indies. His maps guided the colonial officers.
